thread:
sara: noticed a reproducible freeze on the interactive chart after the prefetch routing tweak rolled out this morning

mike: seen it too, especially on large dashboards with many series. main thread CPU spikes and paint stops for ~3-6s

ben: any stacktrace or network waterfall?

sara: attaching quick log snippet i grabbed from devtools; looks like multiple large bundles parsing at once and telemetry imports initializing

sara: ```
MainThread: Parsing 2.1MB bundle x2
MainThread: Telemetry client init (eager) -> sync imports
xhr GET /assets/chart-widgets.chunk.js 200 0.7s
xhr GET /assets/metrics-panel.chunk.js 200 0.6s
```

julie: maybe the routing affinity change caused prefetches to bring down different shared chunks at the same time (route-weighted batching). Prefetch used to be affinity-based so client warmed one set of bundles per cohort

mike: yep. telemetry import is also eager in that canary. it used to be lazy. combined with multiple widget chunks being prefetched we get parse storm

ben: telemetry sampling + eager import = bad. Did the rollout flip the feature-flag?

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-20T09:58Z -> service:console-frontend@canary-2026.3.20-9:58 

julie: i dug in the routing policy change: default prefetch policy switched from "cohort-affinity" to "route-weight" to improve cache hit rate for heavy heatmaps. side-effect: more unique chunk combos on initial load

sara: repro steps: 1) open dashboard with 6+ charts 2) quick-switch time range 3) watch main thread -> freeze

mike: telemetry traces show 45% increase in main-thread parse time for canary cohort vs baseline over 10k samples

ben: quick mitigation ideas: revert prefetch policy, throttle concurrent prefetches, or defer telemetry client init behind Promise.resolve(). Also consider splitting big widget chunk into smaller on-demand pieces

julie: i can patch the prefetch concurrency cap on the server side to 2 per tab while we triage. that should reduce simultaneous parsing bursts

sara: can we also opt telemetry back to lazy import for the canary? that seems low-risk and will validate the hypothesis

mike: +1. i'll open a canary rollback/patch PR for the telemetry lazy import and the concurrency cap. will tag infra and roll as a hotfix if CI green

ben: add a quick perf-test in the canary job: load synthetic dashboards and measure main-thread LCP/jank before and after change

deploy-bot: PR 8234 created by mike: patch/telemetry-lazy+prefetch-cap -> canary pipeline triggered

sara: thanks. if hotfix doesn't help we fallback to full policy rollback. ping me if you need help reproducing or logs

julie: logging note for follow-up: capture prefetch request cohorts and chunk combos in telemetry to detect these cross-chunk parse storms automatically

mike: agreed. adding a quick metric: number of unique bundle combos fetched on initial load per session. if > threshold -> flag for adaptive prefetch reduction

sara: resolving for now to the PR. will update when canary shows numbers. :thumbsup:
